title: Sunny and the Crescent Moon | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka notices tonight's moon is only a tiny crescent — a bright silver smile in the dark sky — and decides the moon must be very happy indeed. A warm bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Something was different about the moon tonight.

Sunny looked up and blinked.

The moon was thin. Not round and full like it usually was. Just a sliver — a crescent, curving like a little silver boat, hanging in the dark navy sky.

Sunny tilted her head.

It looked like a smile.

A big, bright, very comfortable smile. Like the moon was the happiest thing in the whole night sky.

Maybe it is happy, Sunny thought. Maybe the moon has something good to dream about tonight.

The crescent glowed warmly — not as bright as a full moon, but somehow more special. Gentler. A private kind of light.

Around it, the stars were brighter than usual. With the moon smaller, the dark between the stars was deeper, and the stars themselves sparkled more clearly.

Sunny walked out into the open and held her arms slightly out to her sides and turned in a slow circle, looking at all of it.

The smiling moon. The bright stars. The deep dark in between.

She turned and turned until she was slightly dizzy and then sat down, still smiling.

She thought: I think I am happy too.

She lay back in the soft grass and looked up at the crescent moon.

It glowed back at her, steady and warm and smiling.

And she fell asleep to that smile, feeling happy and held and small in the very best way.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, crescent moon. Goodnight, little one.
